title: Review of c14's mwall gate-work finding: on fresh seed 5 the M-gated cells are fixed-width rods while the mbeta=0 twin grows large blobs, splits halve (4 vs 8) and escape falls on seeds 5-6, but by 18-22% rather than ~35%
summary: I looked at pack/seed0/sheet.png and radial.png, then re-ran world.py (mbeta 4) with labkit on seed 5 (128^2, 200 frames x 500 steps) and the matched ablation world_b0.py (the same file with mbeta=0.0; world.py does not read WORLD_P, so an override would be silently ignored) on the same seed. With the gate the cells become rods of roughly constant width from t~22000 (rerun/seed5/sheet.png); without it they grow into large irregular blobs (mbeta0/seed5/sheet.png). labkit: persistent splits 4 (generation 1) vs 8 (generation 2), M rim/core 3.74 vs 3.28 and rim/outside 8.53 vs 3.88 (123/138 vs 120/131 membrane-like). transfer.py (T=15000) on seeds 5 and 6: escape per in-cell particle per 1000 t 0.77/0.74 with the gate vs 0.93/0.95 without (-18%/-22%), transfers 0/0 vs 3.6e-5/0. The particle count is much lower with the gate (N 5322/5498 vs 9351/9559 at t=15000), which the finding does not mention.

observations.B: rerun/seed5/sheet.png vs mbeta0/seed5/sheet.png t>=22000: fixed-width rods vs large blobs; tr_s5_*.txt and tr_s6_*.txt: escape 0.77/0.74 vs 0.93/0.95 per 1000 t; labkit persistent splits 4 vs 8

not_checked: selection on births and deaths (yield percentiles; I did not run the genealogy)

seeds_run.result: pass: rods vs blobs, 4 vs 8 persistent splits, escape 0.77 vs 0.93

controls_run.B: mbeta0/seed5 (world_b0.py, mbeta=0, same seed) and transfer.py mbeta=0 on seeds 5 and 6

verdicts.limitation: The escape reduction is smaller on my seeds (18-22%) than reported (33-38%), and the gate also nearly halves the particle count (about 5400 vs 9400), so lower escape and slower turnover may partly come from fewer particles rather than from containment alone. world.py ignores WORLD_P, so ablations must edit the file. One fresh labkit seed.
